recent_articles.title: Bengali actors face heat after power shift to BJP; FIR filed over 2021 social media posts linked to post-poll violence - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Parambrata Chatterjee**, a Bengali actor, announced he had to align with the **Trinamool Congress** after the recent West Bengal Assembly election results.  He stated this decision was made for his one-year-old son, prompting strong reactions from social media users and fellow actors. **Keya Ghosh**, a BJP leader, responded by criticizing Chatterjee's compromise and highlighting the unwavering support of many BJP supporters in the state.

recent_articles.title: From rallies to reels: political catchphrases turn dance anthems in Kolkata - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A new genre of political techno remixes has emerged in Kolkata, using catchy hooks and meme-friendly punchlines to criticize politicians. The trend began with songs like "Khela Hobe" and continues with remixed versions of "Hamba Hamba", "Mach Chor", and "File Chor". These songs often target specific individuals or parties, gaining popularity through social media platforms like Instagram and YouTube Shorts.  The use of crude humor and satirical lyrics reflects a culture of insult-flinging on social media while also expressing anger towards political leaders who abuse power.

recent_articles.title: One month of Samrat Choudhary Government in Bihar - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Samrat Choudhary**, the leader of the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**, took office as Chief Minister of Bihar on April 15, 2026.  He has implemented several initiatives focusing on development and combating corruption, including a blueprint for 11 satellite townships across 10 districts. The government also launched the "Police Didi Scheme" to enhance women's safety, established a three-tier public support system, and approved significant funding for education and infrastructure projects. Choudhary has also introduced measures to promote transparency in private schools and prioritize local contractors on civil projects.

recent_articles.title: Mamata dons lawyer’s robe, Calcutta HC directs police to ensure safe return of victims affected by violence - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mamata Banerjee**, former West Bengal Chief Minister, appeared before the Calcutta High Court on Thursday, May 14, 2026, alleging police inaction during post-election violence.  She claimed that she is unable to file complaints in person and has been forced to lodge them online. The court directed the **West Bengal police** to ensure safe returns for those illegally evicted from their homes or businesses due to post-election violence.  The Trinamool Congress welcomed the intervention, while protests erupted from a section of lawyers who chanted "chor chor" (thief thief) slogans.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal CM gives sanction to CBI to prosecute officials in several scams - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, West Bengal Chief Minister, granted permission to the **CBI** to prosecute officials involved in teacher's recruitment, municipality recruitment, and cooperative scams.  He stated that these investigations were previously withheld by the previous Trinamool Congress government due to corruption concerns. The move is part of a "zero tolerance" policy against corruption adopted by his BJP-led administration.  The Chief Minister also lifted a ban on potato sales to other states, citing a bumper crop and falling prices.

recent_articles.title: Election results 2026: Why welfare policies aren't winning polls in India like it used to
recent_articles.rephrased_article: India's welfare politics, once a key electoral tool, is facing challenges. While cash transfers and subsidized services have become the norm across parties, recent state elections suggest that extensive welfare delivery alone is no longer enough to secure incumbency.  **Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress**, for example, lost power in West Bengal despite its women-centric welfare schemes. **The Bharatiya Janata Party** has capitalized on expanding welfare architecture, including women's self-help groups and administrative efficiency, while voters are increasingly demanding more than just welfare benefits.  Political scientists argue that this shift signifies a move from the floor of Indian politics to the ceiling, where parties must build coalitions around broader issues like job creation and economic mobility.

recent_articles.title: BJP MLA Tapas Roy sworn in as Pro-tem Speaker of West Bengal Assembly - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tapas Roy**, a senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader and MLA from Maniktala, was sworn in as the Pro-Tem Speaker of the West Bengal Assembly on Tuesday, May 12, 2026. **Suvendu Adhikari**, the Chief Minister, attended the ceremony. The oath-taking of other MLAs will be held on Wednesday and Thursday, with the election for Speaker scheduled for Friday.

recent_articles.title: ECI set to roll out phase III of SIR in ‘coming days’ to cover 22 States, UTs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is set to begin phase three of its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list process in the coming days, covering nearly 40 crore electors across 17 states and five UTs.  This follows completion of SIR in 10 states and three UTs previously, which has successfully removed over 60 lakh deceased voters from the rolls. The ECI had initially delayed the rollout due to Assembly elections in several states but is now proceeding with the revision process.  The exercise aims to ensure accurate voter lists for upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Will hear Trinamool pleas on victory margins being less than deleted votes in SIR, says Supreme Court - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mamata Banerjee**, leader of the **Trinamool Congress**, appeared before the Supreme Court on Monday, May 11, 2026, to argue that deletions made during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in West Bengal affected election results.  Senior advocate Kalyan Bandhopadhyay argued that in some seats, the BJP's victory margin was less than the number of votes deleted. The court asked for an application from **Banerjee** to address the issue and promised to seek information about pending appeals from the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court. The Supreme Court also gave the National Investigation Agency two months to complete its probe into the case of seven judicial officers who were gheraoed in Malda on April 1.

recent_articles.title: Mamata created false narrative on BJP restricting consumption of fish: Dilip Ghosh - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Dilip Ghosh**, newly sworn-in West Bengal minister, attended a fish festival on Sunday (May 10, 2026) and refuted **Mamata Banerjee's** claims that the BJP would restrict consumption of fish and meat if it won the Assembly polls.  He accused Ms. Banerjee of spreading falsehoods during her campaign and claimed the BJP government will promote self-sufficiency in fish production.  Echoing Mr. Ghosh, **Tapas Roy**, the BJP MLA-elect from Maniktala, stated that the previous TMC regime failed to develop the pisciculture sector.

recent_articles.title: Suvendu Adhikari to chair first Cabinet meeting on May 11, 2026 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, the newly elected Chief Minister of **West Bengal**, will hold his first cabinet meeting on Monday, May 11, at Nabanna.  The meeting will see the allocation of portfolios to five ministers who were sworn in with him on Saturday. The cabinet is expected to establish inquiry commissions into atrocities against women during the **Trinamool Congress** regime. Adhikari also plans to meet with top officials from various departments including the police and district magistrates.

recent_articles.title: WB CM Suvendu Adhikari to chair first cabinet meeting today - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, the newly elected Chief Minister of West Bengal, will hold his first cabinet meeting on Monday (May 11, 2026) at Nabanna. The meeting is expected to allocate portfolios to five ministers who were sworn in alongside him on Saturday (May 9). **Adhikari** also plans to establish inquiry commissions into atrocities against women during the previous Trinamool Congress regime and meet with top officials of various departments including police, district magistrates, and the Director General of West Bengal police.

recent_articles.title: Fresh overhaul in Suvendu Adhikari administration likely in near future, say officials - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The newly installed **Suvendu Adhikari**-led BJP government in West Bengal is undertaking a sweeping recalibration of its administrative structure, following the unprecedented scale of pre-poll reshuffle by the Election Commission of India.  **Subrata Gupta**, a retired IAS officer who served as Special Roll Observer during the ECI's exercise, was appointed Advisor to the CM, while **Shantanu Bala**, an Additional District Magistrate, was appointed Private Secretary to the CM. The government also reassigned at least 46 WBCS (Executive) officers and transferred 16 officers from the Chief Minister’s Office, signaling a broader realignment of power corridors in Bengal's bureaucracy.  These changes are seen as part of a larger effort to reshape the state apparatus under the new BJP dispensation.

recent_articles.title: Muslim population in India may match that of Indonesia after Census: Kiren Rijiju - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kiren Rijiju**, Union Minister for Minority Affairs, stated that the Muslim population in India is projected to be nearly equal to Indonesia's population after the upcoming Census. He also expressed concerns over the declining Parsi community and dismissed claims of minority threats, emphasizing equality under the Indian Constitution. **Rijiju** highlighted the BJP's victory in West Bengal as a positive development for national security, citing its border proximity to Bangladesh and concerns about illegal migration.

recent_articles.title: Suvendu Adhikari | The Bengal pivot - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, a prominent Trinamool Congress leader, defected to the **BJP** in December 2020 after several senior party members attempted to persuade him to stay.  Adhikari's decision was driven by his ambition to become West Bengal's Chief Minister, an aspiration he felt unattainable within the **Trinamool Congress**. His departure came as a significant blow to the party, especially with the emergence of **Abhishek Banerjee**, Mamata Banerjee's nephew, who had gained prominence in the political landscape.

recent_articles.title: Sheikh Hasina, Awami League congratulate Suvendu Adhikari - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sheikh Hasina**, former Prime Minister of Bangladesh, congratulated **Suvendu Adhikari**, the new Chief Minister of West Bengal.  The **Bangladesh Awami League**, banned in Bangladesh, expressed support for Mr. Adhikari and stated that they believe this new chapter will elevate relations between Bangladesh and India. The Awami League was banned following a crackdown on civilians in 2024.

recent_articles.title: Trinamool nominates Sobhandeb as Opposition leader, Firhad as Chief Whip - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Trinamool Congress** nominated **Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay**, 82, as the Leader of Opposition in the 18th West Bengal Legislative Assembly.  The party will have two deputy leaders of opposition: **Asima Patra** and **Nayna Bandyopadhya**. **Firhad Hakim** has been appointed as the Trinamool Chief Whip. The decision comes after **Mamata Banerjee** lost her seat in the recent Assembly elections.

recent_articles.title: Naidu and Pawan congratulate Suvendu Adhikari on taking oath as West Bengal CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **N. Chandrababu Naidu**, **Prime Narendra Modi**, and **K. Pawan Kalyan**  attended the swearing-in ceremony of **Suvendu Adhikari** as Chief Minister of West Bengal in Kolkata. **Naidu** congratulated the new government and expressed his best wishes for its success, while **Pawan Kalyan** highlighted the significance of the BJP's victory in addressing concerns about violence, lawlessness, and national security.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal Cabinet 2026: From Dilip Ghosh to Agnimitra Paul, Ministers who were sworn in along with Suvendu Adhikari - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, newly sworn in as the Chief Minister of West Bengal, inducted five new ministers into his cabinet on Saturday. The swearing-in ceremony was attended by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Union Ministers Amit Shah, Rajnath Singh, J. P. Nadda, and Dharmendra Pradhan**, among other BJP leaders.  **Dilip Ghosh**, a senior BJP leader who secured victory in the Kharagpur seat, **Agnimitra Paul**, a fashion designer-turned-legislator who won Asansol Dakshin, **Ashok Kirtania**, a BJP stalwart who gained victory in Bangaon Uttar, and **Kshudiram Tudu**, a former school teacher from Ranibandh (ST) constituency, were among the newly appointed ministers.  **Nisith Pramanik**, a key face of BJP from North Bengal, was also inducted into the cabinet.

recent_articles.title: Abhishek questions credibility of Bengal's electoral process, accuses ECI of being 'partisan' - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Abhishek Banerjee**, senior **TMC** leader, criticized the **Election Commission of India** for alleged partisan conduct and irregularities in the West Bengal Assembly elections won by the **BJP**. He claimed that nearly 30 lakh voters were disenfranchised from the electoral rolls and demanded a transparent count of VVPAT slips.  Banerjee also alleged post-poll violence, attacks on party offices, and intimidation of supporters, calling for an investigation into these incidents. The TMC leader vowed to continue fighting for democracy and the rights of the people under **Mamata Banerjee's** leadership.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal oath-taking LIVE: Suvendu Adhikari sworn in as first BJP CM of West Bengal, five other MLAs also take oath - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, the newly sworn-in BJP Chief Minister of West Bengal, was inaugurated by Governor R.N. Ravi alongside five other MLAs who will join his cabinet. The ceremony was attended by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and senior members of the NDA, including ministers from the Central Government and other state chief ministers.  Post-election violence has erupted in the state since the results were announced on May 4th, with Adhikari's personal assistant being shot dead on May 6th.

recent_articles.title: BJP names Suvendu Adhikari West Bengal chief minister
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, a former aide of **Mamata Banerjee**, has been chosen as the next chief minister of West Bengal by the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**.  The BJP won a landslide victory in the state elections, ending 15 years of rule by **Banerjee's All India Trinamool Congress (TMC)**. Adhikari's rise to power is marked by his controversial political career and his shift from a close ally of **Banerjee** to a leading figure within the BJP.  He will now face challenges including post-election violence, economic concerns, and deep political divisions in the state.

recent_articles.title: Punjab worse than West Bengal under AAP rule, says Haryana CM Saini - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini** criticized the **AAP government in Punjab**, accusing it of failing to control drug trafficking, illegal mining, and lawlessness. He compared the current situation in Punjab to West Bengal under **Mamata Banerjee**, stating that people are disillusioned with the AAP and seeking change through the BJP's governance model.  Saini also contrasted the BJP's policies with those of the Congress, highlighting the latter's corruption and lack of focus on people's welfare.

recent_articles.title: ​Take east: On the BJP government in West Bengal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** secured a resounding victory in the West Bengal Assembly elections, winning 207 out of 294 seats.  **Suvendu Adhikari**, former Leader of the Opposition and now the new Chief Minister, defeated incumbent **Mamata Banerjee** in her own constituency, marking a significant shift in power dynamics. The BJP's success can be attributed to its strategic focus on booth-level organization, leveraging Hindu identity politics, and exploiting popular dissatisfaction with the TMC's governance.  The party's victory comes with challenges, including restoring law and order after targeted violence.

recent_articles.title: BJP’s victory in Bengal will plug a big hole in national security, says Amit Shah - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Amit Shah**, **Union Home Minister**, stated that the BJP's victory in West Bengal was significant for national security, as it plugs a major hole and will make infiltration and cattle smuggling impossible. He emphasized that this victory signifies ideological continuity for the party, marking its presence across all states from Gangotri to Gangasagar.  **Shah** also highlighted the importance of the victory in light of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's 150th birth anniversary and thanked voters for their support. The BJP Legislature Party leader, **Suvendu Adhikari**, will be sworn in as the Chief Minister on May 9th.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal government formation LIVE: Amit Shah arrives in Kolkata for BJP legislature party meet to elect new CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The BJP legislature party** will meet in Kolkata on Friday, May 8, 2026, to elect its leader with **Suvendu Adhikari** emerging as the frontrunner.  Following the BJP's historic victory in the West Bengal Assembly elections, ending the **TMC’s** 15-year rule, **Mamata Banerjee**, the current Chief Minister, has refused to resign and accused the verdict of being a result of a conspiracy. Post-election violence has also erupted across the state since the election results were announced on May 4, 2026, with **Suvendu Adhikari’s** personal assistant being shot dead by unidentified gunmen on Wednesday, May 6, 2026.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal Governor dissolves State Legislative Assembly - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **R. N. Ravi**, the Governor of West Bengal, dissolved the state's Legislative Assembly on May 7, 2026, ending the 17th assembly term. The move follows the BJP's victory in the recent assembly elections, securing a majority and leading to the end of **Mamata Banerjee**'s Trinamool Congress rule.  The swearing-in ceremony for the new BJP government is scheduled for Saturday, May 9, 2026, at the Brigade Parade Grounds.

recent_articles.title: Tensions high in West Bengal after BJP aide shot dead and hundreds arrested | India | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following the BJP's victory in the West Bengal elections, **Tensions** have escalated with violence erupting and hundreds arrested.  **Chandranath Rath**, an aide to the BJP leader **Suvendu Adhikari**, was shot dead, prompting accusations of political killings by the **TMC**, who allege widespread irregularities. The state police chief has registered over 200 criminal cases and arrested 433 individuals for their involvement in post-election violence.  The **BJP** denies all allegations of wrongdoing while the **TMC** vows to challenge the election results in the Supreme Court.

recent_articles.title: Bangladesh seeks China support for Teesta restoration project - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bangladesh**’s new government has sought **China's** involvement in the Teesta River restoration project, a move that could strain relations with **India**.  The **Bangladesh** government is seeking to increase its share of the river's water under the 2011 Teesta water-sharing treaty, which has been blocked by **West Bengal**’s outgoing Chief Minister, **Mamata Banerjee**.  **China's** Foreign Minister, **Wang Yi**, pledged support for **Bangladesh's** new government and its development goals.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal election: Suvendu Adhikari's aide Chandranath Rath shot dead in post-poll violence
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chandranath Rath**, personal assistant to **Suvendu Adhikari**, a top BJP leader, was shot and killed in West Bengal after the state election.  Police are investigating but haven't made any arrests. The incident is part of escalating tensions following the BJP's historic victory, which ended 15 years of rule by **Mamata Banerjee**'s Trinamool Congress (TMC).  The TMC condemned the killing and demanded accountability for those responsible. Both parties have accused each other of violence and intimidation, with the BJP alleging a deterioration in law and order under **Banerjee**. The new chief minister is expected to be sworn in on Saturday.

recent_articles.title: Motorbike gunmen kill BJP political aide in India's West Bengal - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chandranath Rath**, a political aide to **Suvendu Adhikari**, the leader of the opposition in West Bengal's assembly, was shot and killed on Wednesday near his home in Kolkata.  Rath was ambushed by gunmen on motorbikes who opened fire on his vehicle, resulting in multiple gunshot wounds. The killing is the latest in a series of violent incidents since the results of the state elections were announced last week. **Pritam Sengupta**, a doctor at Apollo Hospital, confirmed Rath's death.  The BJP has accused the **All India Trinamool Congress (TMC)** of responsibility for the murder, while the TMC denies any involvement and accuses the BJP of targeting their supporters.

recent_articles.title: Killing as revenge for Mamata’s loss in Bhabanipur: Mother of slain aide of Suvendu - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chandranath Rath’s** mother demanded life imprisonment for the assailants who killed her son after he was shot by bike-borne attackers near Doltala in Madhyamgram. She claimed the killing was a result of **Mamata Banerjee**'s defeat against **Suvendu Adhikari** in Bhabanipur and that TMC leaders had made statements suggesting retribution for BJP workers following the election results.

recent_articles.title: Slain Chandranath Rath: From air force serviceman to Suvendu’s trusted troubleshooter - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chandranath Rath**, a close aide of **Suvendu Adhikari**, the leader of the opposition in West Bengal, was shot dead on Wednesday night.  Rath had served in the Indian Air Force for nearly two decades before transitioning into political coordination and administrative roles. He joined **Adhikari's** inner circle around 2019 after a brief stint in the corporate sector. Rath played a key role in several high-profile political battles, including the BJP’s Bhabanipur campaign, and was considered a trusted confidant of **Adhikari**.  His death has sparked strong reactions in Bengal and heightened tensions following the Assembly election results.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal CM refuses to resign after poll defeat - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mamata Banerjee**, the chief minister of West Bengal, refused to resign after her party lost power in state elections to the **BJP**.  The BJP secured over two-thirds of the seats, marking a significant political milestone for the party. **Banerjee** claimed that 100 seats were "forcibly taken" from her party and accused the **Election Commission** of bias. The **Chief Electoral Officer**, **Manoj Kumar Agarwal**, dismissed these allegations as baseless.  The state's governor can demand Banerjee's resignation or wait until her term ends, at which point a new government will be formed.

recent_articles.title: ‘Defeated by conspiracy’: West Bengal chief minister refuses to resign after election loss | India | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mamata Banerjee**, India's most powerful female politician, has refused to resign as chief minister of West Bengal despite the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** winning a landslide victory in state elections.  Banerjee claims the election was "looted" by conspiracy and that she will not step down. The governor of West Bengal has threatened to send police if Banerjee does not voluntarily relinquish her position, potentially leading to legal challenges. The BJP has responded with accusations of "constitutional blasphemy" and a ban on advisors appointed by Banerjee from entering their offices.  Banerjee's refusal to step down could lead to further political turmoil in the state.

recent_articles.title: Four killed in post-election violence in India’s West Bengal | Elections News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following the **Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s** Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) sweeping victory in West Bengal's state election, at least four people have been killed in political unrest. The BJP claimed two of its workers were killed while the **All India Trinamool Congress (TMC)** party reported two of their workers being beaten to death.  The violence erupted after the results were announced and included clashes between rival supporters in Kolkata and other districts, with allegations of vandalism and attacks on party offices from both sides. The Election Commission of India (ECI) has directed state officials to enforce “zero tolerance” towards post-poll violence.

recent_articles.title: What happens if a Chief Minister refuses to relinquish office after electoral defeat? - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following the BJP's victory in the West Bengal elections, **Mamata Banerjee**, chairperson of the **Trinamool Congress**, refused to resign as Chief Minister, claiming the results were a result of a conspiracy.  She stated that the election was not conducted fairly and accused the BJP of misusing central forces. However, legal experts suggest that an election petition can be filed challenging the results based on allegations of voter deletion during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in West Bengal. The tenure of the current Assembly ends on May 7, at which point a new government will be formed.

recent_articles.title: 4 killed in post-poll unrest in India's West Bengal - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following the **Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s** Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) victory in West Bengal state elections, clashes between rival supporters erupted in Kolkata.  The BJP claimed two of their workers were killed while the **All India Trinamool Congress (TMC)** reported two of their workers were beaten to death. Police confirmed four deaths in clashes and one officer was shot.

recent_articles.title: BJP gears up to pick Bengal CM; Suvendu Adhikari front runner - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Amit Shah**, **Union Home Minister**, has been appointed as the central observer for the election of the leader of the Legislature Party in West Bengal, with **Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi** named co-observer. The BJP is set to form a government after winning 207 seats in the Assembly election, ending the Trinamool Congress's 15-year rule.  **Suvendu Adhikari**, who defeated **Mamata Banerjee** from Bhabanipur, is considered the frontrunner for the post of Chief Minister. The swearing-in ceremony is expected to take place on May 9th with Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** expected to attend.

recent_articles.title: Mamata Banerjee, West Bengal election results 2026: India’s fiercest female politician faces a fight for survival
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mamata Banerjee**, the fierce leader of India's **Trinamool Congress (TMC)** party, suffered a defeat in the West Bengal state elections, ending her bid for a fourth consecutive term as chief minister.  Her loss marks a significant shift in the political landscape of the region and raises questions about her future. The victory of the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** signals a potential power shift and could lead to internal divisions within the TMC. Banerjee's legacy, built on street protests and a commitment to the common man, is now facing uncertainty as she navigates this new political reality.

recent_articles.title: Put petty politics aside, says Rahul Gandhi, as he backs Mamata Banerjee - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, criticized the **BJP's** victory in the West Bengal and Assam Assembly elections as a "theft" of the popular mandate, alleging it marks a step towards destroying Indian democracy. He expressed support for the Trinamool Congress (TMC) and cautioned against political schadenfreude over the party's defeat.  Gandhi urged political parties to prioritize India above partisan considerations.

recent_articles.title: Put petty politics aside, says Rahul Gandhi, as he backs Mamata Banerjee - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, criticized the **BJP's** victory in the West Bengal and Assam Assembly elections as a "theft" of the popular mandate, alleging it was part of the party's attempt to destroy Indian democracy.  He expressed support for the Trinamool Congress (TMC) and urged political parties to prioritize national interests over partisan concerns. **Gandhi** also noted that this is not an isolated incident, referencing previous instances of electoral manipulation by the **BJP**.

recent_articles.title: What Modi’s big win in Indian state elections could mean for its democracy | Elections News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won the West Bengal state assembly elections, marking a significant victory for the party and raising concerns about potential authoritarianism. The BJP's win comes after a history of religious cleavages in the state, but also amidst accusations of voter suppression targeting Muslims.  Actor Joseph Vijay won the Tamil Nadu Assembly election, breaking a long-standing duopoly by the Dravidian parties. In Kerala, the Communist party lost to an alliance led by the Congress. The BJP's consolidation of power has grown with its victories in 21 out of 28 states, raising questions about India's future political landscape and democratic processes.

recent_articles.title: Requiem for Stalin’s spirit - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Joseph Stalin's** spirit appears to be perplexed and saddened by recent events in India, where his former followers have aligned with Hindu nationalism. The Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M) has seen a decline in its influence, with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) gaining significant ground in West Bengal elections.  The CPI-M's support for Hindu nationalist forces is a surprise to Stalin's spirit, who would have preferred a more socialist approach. The writer notes that this shift reflects a broader trend of Indian communists aligning with Hindutva forces, a development that Stalin likely did not anticipate.

recent_articles.title: Assembly Election 2026 results LIVE: TN, Kerala, West Bengal head into Govt formation mode - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mamata Banerjee**, **M.K. Stalin**, and **Pinarayi Vijayan** have lost their respective elections, paving the way for new governments in **Tamil Nadu**, **West Bengal**, and **Kerala**. The BJP secured a landslide victory in West Bengal, while **Vijay**'s TVK party emerged as the single-largest party in Tamil Nadu.  The saffron party also retained Assam and will be part of the incumbent NDA government in Puducherry.

recent_articles.title: ​Lost and found: The Hindu Editorial on the 2026 Assembly elections - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The 2026 Assembly elections in Assam, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry resulted in significant shifts in India's political landscape. The BJP secured victories in Assam and Puducherry while the Congress suffered its worst performance in Assam. In West Bengal, the BJP capitalized on long-term planning and a tainted election process to achieve a decisive victory.  The TVK led by actor C.
